item.title: Rubio, Bessent took decoy Air Force One, Hegseth flew on secret flight with Trump
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were on the decoy flight last month when President Trump secretly switched to a different plane while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was with Mr. Trump.

item.title: Eli Lilly takes aim at illicit market for its experimental weight-loss drug
item.description: The pharmaceutical company is filing lawsuits against six outlets selling versions of its promising but unapproved weight-loss drug, retatrutide.

item.title: 2 killed after Apache helicopter from Fort Hood crashes in Salado, Texas
item.description: Two people aboard an AH-64 Apache attack helicopter based out of Fort Hood were killed in a crash on Wednesday, according to local authorities and the Army.

item.title: Surrogate gives birth to baby at center of multi-state legal battle
item.description: Surrogate McKenna West declined to get an abortion requested by the intended parents after the baby she was carrying was diagnosed with a severe but treatable heart defect.

item.title: Student injured in shooting at Georgia high school, officials say
item.description: One student was injured in a shooting Wednesday afternoon on the campus of a high school in Warner Robins, Georgia, officials said. A suspect is in custody.

item.title: Farm linked to cyclosporiasis outbreak has not been inspected since 2019
item.description: The Mexican lettuce farm linked to the cyclosporiasis outbreak has not been inspected by American regulators in seven years. Dr. Kali Kniel, chair of microbial food safety at the University of Delaware, joins CBS News with more.

item.title: Karoline Leavitt exiting as White House press secretary
item.description: President Trump said Karoline Leavitt will be leaving her role to focus on her young family.

item.title: Judge calls breaks after Lindsay Clancy sobs during murder trial: "I can't do it"
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial was paused multiple times Wednesday afternoon as she sobbed loudly and said "I can't do it" during testimony.

item.title: Surrogate fights parents over baby with heart condition
item.description: A surrogacy case in Texas is raising questions about who decides treatment for a baby - the intended parents or the surrogate. The child, known as Baby Gabriel, was born on Wednesday after the intended parents of the baby requested that the surrogate undergo an abortion at 20 weeks when they learned that the baby had a rare and serious heart defect. The surrogate refused and traveled to Texas. CBS News reporter Shawna Mizelle has the latest and Alexis Cirel, a founding partner of the fertility law practice at SSRGA, has more.

item.title: Europe sees first total solar eclipse in 27 years | Special Report
item.description: Europe on Wednesday experienced its first solar eclipse in nearly three decades. Lindsey Reiser anchored CBS News' special coverage.

item.title: Karoline Leavitt says she's leaving her role as press secretary
item.description: Karoline Leavitt announced Wednesday that she will be departing her role as press secretary at the end of the month. CBS News White House reporter Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: U.S. indicts former SPLC executive for her role in alleged fraud scheme
item.description: Prosecutors have accused the Southern Poverty Law Center of telling donors and banks it was dismantling white supremacist and extremist groups, while funneling payments to confidential informants in the groups.

item.title: Recapping Europe's total solar eclipse, first in nearly 3 decades
item.description: Europe on Wednesday saw its first total solar eclipse in 27 years. CBS News' Bill Harwood shares his thoughts on the event and Derrick Pitts, chief astronomer at the Franklin Institute in Philadelphia, joins to discuss.

item.title: Total solar eclipse darkens skies across Northern Hemisphere
item.description: The only total solar eclipse of 2026 crossed the Northern Hemisphere today, with a path of totality across parts of Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain. See photos and video from the best viewing locations.

item.title: Trump says U.S. has "total control" over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday that the U.S. has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, writing on social media: "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT."

item.title: The ins and outs of egg freezing | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez began sharing on social media that she is going to try to preserve her fertility by freezing her eggs, a subject that Lesley Stahl reported on in 2025. Stahl found that the costly procedure brought happy endings to some women, but offered no guarantees.

item.title: Nick Reiner indicted on murder charges in parents' killings at their LA home
item.description: Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder with the special circumstance allegations in the killings of his parents, Rob and Michele Reiner.

item.title: Credit card balances just rose by $21 billion. Here's how to get your debt forgiven now.
item.description: Credit card balances rose again in the second quarter of 2026. Here's how to get your debt forgiven right now.

item.title: Astronomy professor breaks down how eclipses work: "We get the best eclipses in the solar system"
item.description: Janna Levin, professor of physics and astronomy at Barnard College, joins CBS News to discuss Wednesday's total solar eclipse.

item.title: ICE plans to give officers gloves that can deliver electric shocks
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers may soon be outfitted with gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks that are intended to gain compliance from combative individuals.

item.title: Witnesses describe total solar eclipse: "Absolutely amazing"
item.description: Europe saw its first total solar eclipse in 27 years on Wednesday. CBS News' Rob Marciano was in Mallorca, Spain, for the moment of totality and spoke with some of the people who saw it.

item.title: Norah O'Donnell: I take testosterone. Here's why.
item.description: Norah O'Donnell sat down with her own doctor, Rachel Rubin, to tackle the important topic of menopause: How your body changes, why women may be needlessly suffering, and what you can actually do about it.

item.title: Maps and charts show record number of measles cases in U.S. this year
item.description: CBS News has been tracking a record number of measles cases and outbreaks around the country. The majority of cases are among those who haven't been vaccinated.

item.title: Watch: Cheers in Spain during solar eclipse's moment of totality
item.description: CBS News' Rob Marciano reports from Mallorca, Spain, on the moment of totality during Wednesday's solar eclipse.

item.title: How the Secret Service is cracking down on card-skimming scams
item.description: A Secret Service analyst told CBS News a single skimming device can net a scammer up to $1 million.

item.title: Aid worker describes situation in Colombia after earthquake: "Things are not good here"
item.description: Diana Gutiérrez de Piñeres Botero, Americares Colombia country director, joins CBS News from Bogotá, Colombia, to discuss the situation on the ground there after Tuesday's massive earthquake.

item.title: How much time does AI save at work? New Census Bureau data breaks it down.
item.description: New Census data shows how much faster workers can complete tasks when they enlist artificial intelligence for help.

item.title: 11 charged for alleged sham marriages to help Chinese nationals get green cards
item.description: The DOJ unveiled criminal charges alleging 11 people participated in a scheme that involved more than 1,000 "sham marriages" between Chinese nationals and U.S. citizens.

item.title: Farm linked to cyclosporaisis outbreak went years without FDA inspection
item.description: The FDA has long fallen short of legally required inspection targets, and foreign inspections fell further last year amid agency layoffs.

item.title: Baby rescued from earthquake rubble in Colombia as death toll rises
item.description: Footage shared on social media shows a baby being rescued from the bloody arms of a man trapped underneath a destroyed building in Cali after a powerful earthquake struck Colombia.
